# Palette v0.4: a colour system from the logo hue (asks 11 and 12, round 2)

**Two options, P1 and P2, generated by one script from the logo's hue. I recommend P1. Reply P1 or P2.**

- **P1 Complementary.** This is 12A made systematic. It keeps the warm paper, the clay accent and the warm Today bars against the cool blue.
- **P2 Rectangle.** This is the bolder, redder option.
- **The charts are restyled in both options.** The colours were only part of why the first charts looked heavy (see section 4).
- **Your browser pass is still needed.** Every picture comes from the real app with real ECharts charts, but the review was on screenshots, not in your browser.

All figures are invented placeholders, not quotes. Nothing in `mock/src`, `mock/public` or `spec.md` was changed.

## 1. The two options

| | **P1 Complementary (recommended)** | **P2 Rectangle** |
|---|---|---|
| Harmony scheme | **Complementary.** The blue sits against the warm half opposite it. The saving is the blue's analogous neighbour. | **Tetradic rectangle.** It uses two complementary pairs: 232°/52° and 152°/332°. |
| Why it suits InfraVana | Warm against cool tells the story: Today is warm and familiar, InfraVana is the one cool, clear mark. A teal saving sits next to the brand, so it reads as InfraVana's result. Earthy warm hues feel trustworthy, not alarming. | The most colourful option. Leaf green is the classic "money kept" signal. Crimson to vermilion is lively and confident. |
| Today (comparator, options 1 to 3) | `#5d1534` wine, `#8f2526` brick, `#a1592a` burnt orange, `#b28439` ochre | `#5f0d40` wine, `#921840` crimson, `#c82521` scarlet, `#d86a26` vermilion |
| InfraVana | `#006c93` | `#006c93` |
| Saved (fill / figure text) | `#319379` / `#1e6250` (teal) | `#349d5b` / `#1e6538` (leaf green) |
| Paper, surface, ink | `#f7f4ef`, `#fcfaf6`, `#1d1c19` (the warm paper of 12A) | `#f2f5f6`, `#f9fafb`, `#191c1e` (near-neutral, close to infravana.ai's `#fafafa`) |
| Section accent (chrome only) | `#7f5a43` clay | `#214d62` quiet navy |
| Selected state | `#dcedf6` fill, `#005d7f` 2px edge | the same |
| Primary button, chosen tab | `#004964`, hover `#003347` | the same |
| Lowest text pair | 4.53 (ink label inside the saved bar) | 4.99 (the same pair) |
| Lowest mark pair | 3.06 (ochre bar on the paper) | 3.13 (green bar on the paper) |
| Smallest CIEDE2000 between two chart fills | normal 17.5, deuteranopia 11.5, protanopia 14.3, tritanopia 11.8 | normal 13.4, deuteranopia 11.7, protanopia 10.1, tritanopia 12.4 |
| **What you give up** | **The brightest charts.** The ochre and burnt orange are earthy, not bright. The four Today bars share one warm family, so they are told apart by lightness first and hue second. | **Calm.** Crimson and scarlet are the loudest colours on the page, and red reads as cost or alarm, which works against the hopeful register. The scarlet bar outshouts InfraVana's blue at a glance. |

**Why I recommend P1:**
- It keeps everything you liked in 12A and fixes what was arbitrary in it (section 3).
- Every Today step is equal.
- No Today bar is more saturated for its hue than InfraVana.
- It is the calmer of the two, and still clearly colourful.

**Only two options, not three.** The same script built two more schemes, and the checks rejected both (section 5). Every scheme that keeps six fills at least 10 apart in all three colour-vision deficiencies has the same structure:
- InfraVana in blue.
- The saving in green or teal.
- Today in the red-to-yellow half, darkest at the red end.

So the options differ in where Today sits on that arc and how vivid it is, in the saving's hue, and in the chrome.

## 2. Method, step by step (every value comes from these rules)

1. **Sample the logo.** `python3 -I -B sample_logo.py` decodes `mock/public/logo.jpeg` with macOS `sips`.
   - It keeps the 125,476 logo pixels whose OKLCH chroma is at least 0.02 and whose lightness is under 0.90. The background is about `#f9f9f9`, at chroma about 0.
   - Median: **L 0.557, C 0.038, h 231.9°** (`#5e7886`). Circular mean hue 232.5°. The 10th to 90th percentile of the hue is 221.3° to 243.8°.
   - **Base hue: 232°.** The logo itself is not touched.
2. **Colour space: OKLCH** (Ottosson 2020), so that equal steps in L, C and h look equal.
   - Values outside sRGB keep their L and h and lose chroma (binary search).
   - `generated/palettes.json` records both the chroma asked for and the chroma reached.
3. **Hue: the base plus each scheme's offsets.**

   | Role | P1 offset (resulting hue) | P2 offset (resulting hue) |
   |---|---|---|
   | InfraVana | 0 (232°) | 0 (232°) |
   | Saved | −60 (172°, teal) | +280 (152°, the green vertex) |
   | Today: comparator, option 1, option 2, option 3 | +127, then steps of 26 (359°, 25°, 51°, 77°) | +116, then steps of 20 (348°, 8°, 28°, 48°): the warm side between the vertices 332° and 52° |
   | Paper, rules, ink | +213 (85°, the yellow end of the arc) | 0 (232°) |
   | Section accent | +180 (52°, the complement) | 0 (232°) |

4. **Lightness ladders (OKLCH L), with equal steps.**
   - **Today:** 0.33, 0.435, 0.54, 0.645 (steps of 0.105).
     - Lightness rises as the hue moves from red toward yellow. This is the natural order of hues: a dark yellow turns olive or brown, and a light red turns pink. That is why the arc starts at wine and ends at ochre rather than being centred on the complement. Centred, it gave muddy browns, and its best CIEDE2000 minimum was 9.5.
     - The darkest rung (0.33) is the darkest at which a red still reads as a colour.
     - The lightest rung (0.645) is the lightest that still reaches 3:1 on the paper.
   - **Brand:** InfraVana 0.50, InfraVana text 0.45, button 0.38, button hover 0.30.
   - **Saved:** fill 0.60 in P1 and 0.62 in P2; figure text 0.45.
   - **Chrome:** paper 0.968, surface 0.985, muted 0.935, grid 0.905, border 0.865, strong border 0.62, secondary text 0.47, ink 0.225.
   - **Selected row:** 0.935. Section accent: 0.50 in P1, 0.40 in P2. P2's accent is one brand step darker so that it reads as chrome: it is 11.4 CIEDE2000 from the InfraVana bar.
5. **Chroma budget: chrome low, marks high, InfraVana the highest for its hue.**
   - **Chrome:** absolute OKLCH C.
     - Paper: 0.007 in P1, 0.003 in P2.
     - Ink: 0.006. Rules: 0.012. Selected tint: 0.022.
     - Section accent: 0.060, about half of any mark's chroma.
   - **Marks:** a share of the sRGB maximum at their own L and h ("relative chroma"). sRGB holds far more chroma for warm hues than for this steel blue: at L 0.5 the blue's maximum is about 0.10, red's is about 0.20.
     - **InfraVana: 100%** (C 0.102). This is as vivid as this hue can be shown.
     - **Saved: 85%.**
     - **Today: 80% in P1, 90% in P2.**
     - So no Today bar is closer to its most vivid version than InfraVana is to its own.
     - In absolute C, some warm bars are higher (P1 brick 0.142). That is the gamut, not the rule. Section 3 shows that 12A broke this rule in relative terms too.
6. **Fixed semantic roles, the same in every chart.**
   - **Today comparator:** the darkest rung, with labels inside the bar in paper.
   - **Today options 1 to 3:** the next rungs, always with a direct label.
   - **Option 4:** not drawn. The Today bars stay at your default of four: the comparator plus three options. A fifth Today bar would need a rung that fails 3:1 (L 0.75) or collides with the comparator.
   - **InfraVana:** the blue.
   - **Saved:** its own hue, with ink labels. The chip colour is chosen by the rule "paper if it reaches 4.5:1, otherwise ink".
   - **Section accent:** chrome only, never in a chart. It colours the step label and its rule, the kickers and the 2px rule over the chart.
   - **Selected state:** a tint of the base hue plus a 2px InfraVana-text edge.
7. **Checks** (`python3 -I -B palette.py --check` exits 1 if any fails):
   - **WCAG 2.x:** 4.5:1 for every text pair and 3:1 for every mark and border pair. There are 38 pairs per option, including the chart chips, the C10 wash and the focus ring.
   - **CIEDE2000:** at least 10 between every two of the six fills in one chart. This is checked under normal vision and under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia (Machado 2009 severity-1 matrices, applied in linear sRGB).
   - **Greyscale:** the relative-luminance ladder.
   - **Section accent:** its distance from the nearest chart fill.
8. **Shipped values match the script.** I built the scratch app (`vite build`) and read the compiled CSS. Each option's block holds exactly the 21 hex values `palette.py` generated, none missing and none extra.

### Results of the checks (full tables in `generated/checks.md`)

| | P1 | P2 | 12A as drawn |
|---|---|---|---|
| WCAG pairs, failures | 38, **0** | 38, **0** | 38, 0 |
| CIEDE2000 minimum: normal | 17.5 | 13.4 | 17.6 |
| deuteranopia | 11.5 | 11.7 | **6.7** (ember against saffron) |
| protanopia | 14.3 | 10.1 | 11.5 |
| tritanopia | 11.8 | 12.4 | 10.7 |
| Greyscale ladder, darkest to lightest (contrast to the next darker step) | comparator, option 1 1.52, InfraVana 1.45, option 2 1.12, Saved 1.40, option 3 1.12 | comparator, option 1 1.50, InfraVana 1.47, option 2 1.05, option 3 1.61, Saved 1.02 | comparator, option 1 1.37, InfraVana 1.31, option 2 1.36, Saved 1.29, option 3 1.04 |
| Section accent against the nearest bar (CIEDE2000) | 10.1 | 11.4 | 5.0 |

**Greyscale caveat (the same as in 12A).** Two neighbours on each ladder are close in grey:
- InfraVana and option 2.
- Saved and option 3 (P1) or option 3 and Saved (P2).

They never need grey to be told apart:
- They sit in different rows with direct labels.
- Saved only ever appears inside the InfraVana row.

I tried moving InfraVana and Saved into the middle of their gaps (L 0.4875 and 0.5925). The saved-bar label then failed 4.5:1 (4.42), so I did not make that change.

## 3. 12A against the rules: what is kept and what is corrected

| 12A as drawn | Measured | P1 |
|---|---|---|
| Warm paper `#f6f4ef`, clay section accent, warm Today against the cool blue | the story you liked | **kept**: paper `#f7f4ef`, clay `#7f5a43`, same story |
| InfraVana `#21678e` | hue 237.7°, 5.8° off the logo's 231.9° | **corrected** to the logo hue exactly: `#006c93` |
| Today lightness 0.367, 0.445, 0.580, 0.643 | uneven steps (0.078, 0.135, 0.063) | **corrected** to equal steps of 0.105 |
| Today hues 357°, 32°, 46°, 77° | uneven steps (35°, 14°, 31°) | **corrected** to equal steps of 26° |
| Ember C 0.149, saffron 0.131, InfraVana 0.092 | the Today bars outshout InfraVana | **corrected** by the chroma budget (InfraVana 100% of its gamut, Today 80%) |
| Ember against saffron under deuteranopia | CIEDE2000 6.7 | **corrected**: smallest pair 11.5 |
| Clay accent `#9a422d` against the brick bar `#8e3021` | CIEDE2000 5.0: the accent reads as a chart series | **corrected** to chrome chroma 0.06: 10.1 from the nearest bar |
| Option 4 reused option 1's colour | CIEDE2000 0.0 | **corrected**: the Today bars are capped at your default of four |

## 4. Why the charts looked ugly, and the fixes (drawn in every board)

The first boards used the same chart styling for 12A, 12B and 12C, so all three failed the same way; colour alone could not fix them. [`01-diagnosis.png`](01-diagnosis.png) marks each fault on the pictures.

| # | Fault | Fix (ECharts option or CSS token) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Slab weight. The bars took 58% of the row (about 31px), wider than the gaps, so five bars read as a wall. | C1 and C5 `barWidth`: 24px fixed, about 30px of air between rows |
| 2 | The y axis rule showed only between the bars, as broken ticks. | `yAxis.axisLine.show: false` |
| 3 | Every row name was bold. | Bold only for the two bars being compared; the other options at `--font-weight-regular` |
| 4 | Each saving had a dark green outline plus a white separator: three framed boxes in one bar. | `--chart-separator-width: 2px`: one gap of paper between every two segments, no outlines (`outlineOf`) |
| 5 | The Today bars were more saturated than InfraVana. | The chroma budget (section 2.5) |
| 6 | A 1.5px ink budget line ran through every gap. | `--chart-budget-line-width: 1px`, `--color-budget-line: var(--color-text-secondary)` (6.2:1) |
| 7 | End labels ("quality 87 · $111K") were all bold. | Rich text: the quality in secondary ink, the dollar figure bold |
| 8 | The section accent looked like a data colour. | Chrome chroma 0.06 |
| 9 | C3: bars up to 96px wide against 12px markers. | `BAR_MAX_PX` 44, `BAR_WIDTH_PCT` 18, `BAR_GAP_PCT` 20, `MARKER_SIZE` 14 |
| 10 | No rhythm in the hues. | Equal ladders (section 2.4) |
| 11 | C10: 8px points with a paper ring broke the frontier into dashes. | `POINT_SIZE` 6 with no ring, `--chart-frontier-line-width: 3px`, a 10% brand wash from the frontier down to the best Today line (`areaStyle.origin`). The wash shows the gain as an area: the label on it is 5.77:1 |
| 12 | C10 Today lines too thin to show their hue. | `--chart-today-line-width: 2px` |
| + | Unlabelled $12.9K saving block on narrow charts | The InfraVana row label adds "· $45.9K saved" in the saving colour |
| + | Chips drawn over the bar's paper gap | `label.backgroundColor: transparent` on solid fills |

The exact change is [`chart-look.patch`](chart-look.patch).
- **What it patches.** The patch is a unified diff against the v0.4 proposal scratch copy (the one with `src/v04.ts`), not against `mock/src`.
- **How it switches on.** Its ECharts option changes are keyed on `?look`, and the token values are in `src/styles/v04look.css`.
- **Check.** It applies cleanly to that copy with `patch -p1`.

## 5. Rejected schemes (in `palette.py` as `REJECTED`, checked by the same run)

| Candidate | Best found | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Triad 232°/352°/112° (Today around 352°, saving at 112°) | CIEDE2000 8.1 under protanopia (comparator against option 1) and 8.7 under deuteranopia (saving against option 3); the saved-bar label is 4.40 | The magentas turn blue for red-green deficient viewers and meet InfraVana. A 112° saving is olive (`#82862b`). |
| Analogous (Today on the blue's neighbours) with a gold saving | CIEDE2000 4.1 under tritanopia (InfraVana against a teal Today) | Blue, teal and indigo collapse for tritanopes. |

These were the best of a grid search over each scheme's free parameters: start hue, hue step, lightness start and step, Today chroma share, InfraVana lightness and the saving's hue and lightness. The search script is not checked in. The parameters it found are in `REJECTED`.

## 6. How the pictures were made

- **Scratch copy.** I copied the scratch app `design-v04/work` (without `node_modules`) to `design-v04/work-palette`, symlinked `node_modules`, and ran Vite on 127.0.0.1:5230 with its cache outside the repo.
  - `playwright-core` drove the installed Chrome headless at 1280 and 390 wide, at 2x.
  - Address: `?a1&a2&a3&a9&a10&a4=B&a5=B&a6=B&a7&a8=C&pal=P1|P2|A[&look]`.
- **Same state in both columns.** 12A and the options use the same app state, so only the colours and the chart styling differ:
  - asks 1, 2, 3, 7, 9 and 10 on;
  - 4B, 5B and 8C, as you chose;
  - 6B stands in for the goal tabs until they are redrawn as browser tabs.
- **Colour-vision renders.** These apply the same Machado matrices as `palette.py`, as an SVG `feColorMatrix` (linear RGB) on the page.
- **What I fixed after looking at the pictures:**
  - bars that were too thin (20px became 24px);
  - chips showing over the paper gap;
  - paper-ringed C10 points cutting the line;
  - a wash that tinted the whole plot (it now stops at the best Today line);
  - a missing saving label on the narrower 8C layout;
  - board columns out of line;
  - diagnosis marks covering labels.

## 7. Notes and open items

- **Your browser pass.** Every picture is a headless render. Hover states and tooltips were not drawn.
- **Logo tile.** The logo JPEG has a `#f9f9f9` background, which shows as a faint tile on both papers (P1 `#f7f4ef`, P2 `#f2f5f6`). The logo stays untouched. The tile is inherited, not introduced.
- **Intake estimate colour.** The intake estimate's "You save 47%" uses the InfraVana colour, not the saving colour. A one-token change in the build would make it `--color-positive`. I did not draw it.
- **Accent change needs sign-off.** Either option changes the accent from `#466577` to `#006c93`. That is a brand-owner decision (spec 12.4), as in the first boards.
- **Spec updates needed.** Spec 14.1 and 14.4 need the chosen option's tokens, the chroma budget, the "four Today bars at most" rule and the chart restyle.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `colour.py` | sRGB, WCAG luminance, OKLab and OKLCH, CIELAB, CIEDE2000, Machado simulation; standard library only |
| `sample_logo.py` | Logo sampling (step 1) |
| `palette.py` | Every rule and parameter. It writes `generated/` and, with `--check`, fails on any check |
| `generated/tokens.css` | The CSS overrides each option loads (`html[data-pal="P1"]`, `"P2"`) |
| `generated/palettes.json` | Every value and check result, machine-readable |
| `generated/checks.md` | Every value and check result as tables |
| `chart-look.patch` | The chart restyle, as a patch to the v0.4 scratch copy |
| `*.png` | The boards listed at the top |

To regenerate: `cd mock/docs/design-v0.4/palette && python3 -I -B sample_logo.py && python3 -I -B palette.py --check`.
